clue.text: Motor-racing substitute in hotspot

parts.note: Formula One, written F1, read here with the figure 1 as the letter I
to substitute is to replace, as a verb

explanation.surface: A stand-in driver is called up at a dangerous racing location.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 (Formula One) is read with its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic hearth is literally the hot spot of a room, a playful description of where the fire burns.

clue.text: Paper takes in initial contributions from criminals and police

parts.note: to take someone in is to deceive or fool them

indicators.note: initial contributions are the opening letters supplied by each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A newspaper is duped by tips passed on by crooks and the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional size of writing or printing sheet, so a kind of paper.

clue.text: Favour having no power to make allusions

indicators.note: having no signals that the following item is taken away from the word

parts.note: to favour one option is to prefer it
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone stripped of influence resorts to hinting rather than acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention or allude to something is a synonym, as in mentioning a matter in passing.

clue.text: Where you go when you get the choice?

definitions.text: Where you go when you get the choice?

parts.words: Where you go when you get the choice?
parts.note: sounds like a lucky moment of freedom, but the choice is a vote at an election

explanation.surface: A question about where to head when given freedom to decide.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters go to a designated building on election day to cast their ballot, exercising their choice.

clue.text: Muscles consequently not hard — not being there!

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles

indicators.note: not here tells the solver to drop the following letter from the word before

parts.note: hence means consequently or therefore
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Weak muscles mean someone simply fails to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence is the state of not being present somewhere, a direct dictionary sense.

clue.text: Historic article used to exist within boundaries of Edinburgh? Nonsense

indicators.note: within puts the following material inside the frame made by the outer letters
the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the definite article, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
was is the past tense of be, meaning existed

explanation.surface: A historic Scottish relic that once existed in Edinburgh is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ye' is the old spelling seen on signs like Ye Olde Tea Shoppe; 'within' puts both pieces between the first and last letters of Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for talk meant to deceive, i.e. rubbish or humbug.

clue.text: Cheat in exam recalled cane? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter at the end is lopped off
recalled, read as called back, tells us to write the word backwards

parts.note: a birch is a rod used for corporal punishment, like a cane

explanation.surface: A teacher remembers caning a pupil caught cheating in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRCH written backwards is HCRIB; 'Not entirely' drops its final letter, H.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a set of notes smuggled in for illicit use in a test.

clue.text: Think back about one's tucking into meat dish

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: tucking into places the item within the word that follows

parts.note: mince is minced meat, a dish in its own right
one is I, and one's is read as one is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the past while eating a meal of mince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' looks like eating, but it is the container signal; 'one's' is read as 'one is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past experiences fondly, synonymous with recollecting.

clue.text: Handle lightly used, turning up amongst these many buildings

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
amongst signals letters found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A name casually used for a cluster of buildings that keeps cropping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amongst' takes EMANYB from 'thesE MANY Buildings'; 'turning up' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A byname is a nickname or secondary name, an informal handle for someone.

clue.text: Treated fish — bit kosher, with aroma that's weird

indicators.note: weird letters are strange ones, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smoked fish that is partly kosher gives off a strange smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Fodder is BITKOSHER plus AROMA; 'weird' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smokie is haddock hot-smoked in the Scottish town of Arbroath, a cured fish.

clue.text: Tripe etc not almost on everything?

indicators.note: on signals one piece placed next to the other

parts.note: off means not happening, as when an event is off rather than on

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A sceptical question about whether tripe is fit for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is stomach lining, one example of animal entrails and organ meats.

clue.text: Navigator provoking mare's-nest

indicators.note: provoking stirs things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A helmsman stirs up an illusory discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: A mare's-nest is a supposed discovery that turns out to be illusory.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who steers a vessel, guiding its course as a navigator does.

clue.text: Some European perplexing European brains

indicators.note: perplexing means confusing, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A European puzzling over another European's intellect.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Serbia is one kind of European national.

clue.text: Mate engaged in some radio broadcasting suggests radar?

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: AM, amplitude modulation, is one method of radio broadcasting
a crony is a close friend or mate

explanation.surface: A friend involved in radio work hints at radar.
explanation.walkthrough: RADAR comes from RAdio Detection And Ranging, hence the question mark for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is formed from the initial letters of a phrase, an example of such a word.

clue.text: Gathered gaol's wrecked in dispute

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prisoners massed together trash the jail during a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning quarrelling or in fierce disagreement.

clue.text: Security expert possibly dreads story on the radio

parts.note: dreadlocks are one possible type of locks of hair

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a myth is a story

explanation.surface: A security expert's hairstyle features in a broadcast tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes and repairs locks works in the field of security.

clue.text: Stormy sea, for me, is terrifying

indicators.note: stormy suggests tossed about, so these letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: Someone confesses rough seas frighten them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means frightening in appearance, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: What generates smile after unhappy tot's kept in confinement? Dairy product

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the first one
kept in means held inside the word for confinement

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement

indicators.note: unhappy here means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: photographers ask you to say cheese to make you smile

explanation.surface: A miserable toddler locked up wonders what would make them smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' rearranges the letters of tot into OTT; the 's of tot's is read as 'is', linking to 'kept in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft white curd from skimmed milk, a dairy food.

clue.text: Getting on when accepting new lists of things to do

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: getting on means growing old, i.e. aged
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: An older person taking on fresh tasks to tick off.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a schedule of items to be handled, plural here.

clue.text: Require space for church

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A demand for room to be made for a church.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure, half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist upon or compel compliance with a rule is to demand or necessitate it.

clue.text: Area of Europe American gets wrong at first

indicators.note: at first means the other piece comes before this letter

parts.note: a crime is a wrong act

explanation.surface: An American misunderstands a European region at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula on the Black Sea is a region of Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Award went down in memory

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: learning by rote is learning from memory
the sun set, meaning it went down

explanation.surface: A prize that sank into memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribboned badge given as a prize at shows.

clue.text: Fine acrobat offering no opening for an incompetent

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: offering no opening means losing the first letter

parts.note: a tumbler is an acrobat who performs somersaults

explanation.surface: A circus performer gives no chance to a bungler.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person who drops things and mishandles tasks is a bungler.

clue.text: Language from some personnel in Government

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The jargon used by civil servants in government.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a foreign tongue or specialist jargon.

clue.text: One parliamentarian appearing in paper, backing purchase scheme

indicators.note: appearing in means set inside another piece
backing means going in reverse, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper
one is I as a Roman numeral
a lord sits in the House of Lords, part of Parliament

explanation.surface: A peer in the newspaper supports a buying scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses only the word for paper, giving MAER; a lord is a parliamentarian as a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of buying goods by post or catalogue is a method of purchase.

clue.text: Martial art to finish in decisive outcome

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: KO, a knockout, decisively ends a boxing match
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A fighting sport bout ending in a conclusive result.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese fencing with bamboo swords is one of the fighting disciplines.

clue.text: The chap appears after analgesic gutted pain

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the first
gutted means the insides removed, leaving the outside letters

parts.note: he refers to the chap

explanation.surface: A man takes a stripped-down painkiller for his pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Docker having day before — and day after — in warehouse

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a store is a warehouse
eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: A dock worker spends the day before and after in a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at the dockside.
